analysis.title: RBC European Rates & Economics Daily
key_insights: US equities posted their biggest single-session rally in over seven months on Monday as AI dip-buyers returned. US futures are marginally higher overnight. Kospi rose 4.4% as tech sentiment recovered.
European equity futures point to a positive open: Euro Stoxx 50 +0.9% at 6,358, DAX +0.9% at 26,590, FTSE 100 +0.6% at 10,869.

Trump signalled further strikes on Iran are unnecessary, which raised hopes for an earlier end to the conflict after the Democrat midterm sweep. Oil sold off sharply and kept falling overnight, with Brent approaching $90.
Trump backed Secretary of War Pete Hegseth as Congress pushes to impeach him over his conduct during the Iran War.
China October CPI eased more than expected on falling food prices. The PBOC is seen as unlikely to cut policy rates near term, with fiscal stimulus the preferred lever.
Japan's 30-year JGB auction barely cleared, which points to fragile demand at the long end.
RBC Economics expects October US CPI at +0.3% m/m for both headline and core. Year-over-year comparisons are unavailable because the government shutdown left October 2025 data missing.

RBC Economics sees September's CPI as showing early energy price spillover, which it views as only the start of broader inflationary pressure. Core goods prices have accelerated for three months on tariffs in apparel and footwear, toys and recreational goods, and IT equipment. Motor vehicle parts prices are starting to feed into used car prices.

RBC Economics expects no meaningful relief in services: housing costs keep rising and super core services inflation, which has never declined y/y, stays sticky. It sees inflation risks skewed heavily to the upside.

Three ECB-related appearances are due Nov 11: Cipollone on the digital euro at the European Parliament's ECON Committee (generally seen as a dove), Escrivá on Europe's positioning in the new geopolitical landscape, and Lane's keynote at the BoE Watchers Conference.

At the BoE and Its Watchers conference, Fed Governor Waller opens, Lane closes, and BoE Deputy Governor Lombardelli gives a keynote. Panels cover geopolitics and monetary policy and debt/fiscal policy.

Lombardelli wrote in last week's MPC minutes that absent evidence of weaker inflation pressures, there is likely a case for a further rate increase in the near term. RBC will watch whether she defines 'near term' and keeps the hawkish tone.
Other speakers: BoE's Breeden at the UBS European Conference, and the Fed's Logan (opening remarks) and Schmid (fireside chat) at the Fed's 11th annual energy conference.
RBC forecasts the Fed funds midpoint rising from 3.88 on Nov 6 to 4.13 in Q4 26 and 4.38 by Q1 27. It forecasts the 10y Treasury yield at 5.40 in Q4 26 against 4.86 on Nov 6.

RBC forecasts the ECB deposit rate rising from 2.50 to 2.75 in Q4 26 and holding. It forecasts the BoE rate at 4.00 in Q4 26 and 4.25 from Q1 27, with the 10y Gilt at 5.25 in Q4 26 against 5.17 on Nov 6.
